messages:
Maya: Ticket #4521 — customer (acme-ml) reporting sporadic p99 spikes on /v1/embeddings; also seeing intermittent "dimension_mismatch" errors when they batch at client side. Pasted original report and minimal repro below.

Customer: "We saw p99 jump from ~120ms to 1.2s under sustained traffic. Also some API responses return 512-d vectors and later 1536-d vectors and our indexer fails: 'dimension_mismatch: expected 1536 got 512'"

Maya: Repro steps they provided:
```
# single request
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model": "embed-small-v1","input": "hello world"}'

# batched: they batch two texts from two users
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model": "embed-small-v1","input": ["a","b"]}'
```
They also send a mix of calls where one request explicitly sets model=embed-large-v2 (migration tests)."

Elena: Customer says issue started after they enabled "auto-size batching" in their client, which groups user-submitted texts into variable-sized batches and sometimes includes requests from a canary they launched.

Arjun: Assigning to eng-ml to triage. @Arjun I'll pull serving traces and batch logs for that org id. Any initial hypotheses:
- dynamic batching combined requests targeted to different model ids/quantizations and our routing allowed compatibility mismatch
- high max_batch_size causing kernel choice that favors throughput but spikes tail latency for small sequences
- batch waiting timeouts tuned too high (waiting to fill larger batches)

Nate: I pulled the trace: for org acme-ml we see model routing flips between `embed-small-v1@quant=8` and `embed-large-v2@fp16` across requests at similar times. Serving logs (snippet):
```
[1748001200] batch_id=342 model_targets=[embed-small-v1@q8, embed-large-v2@fp16] size=3 wait_ms=12 exec_ms=310
[1748001201] batch_id=343 model_targets=[embed-small-v1@q8] size=1 wait_ms=500 exec_ms=80
```
Dimension mismatch arises downstream in their indexer because they assume a single embedding_dim. Error from customer:
`ERROR indexing: dimension_mismatch expected=1536 got=512`

Arjun: Root cause theory — our smart routing + dynamic batching allowed heterogeneous model targets to be considered for the same logical grouping. The runtime currently coalesces requests that are compatible at tokenization level but doesn't enforce identical output dims when requests come from different model pins. The mismatch shows when the customer mixes `embed-small-v1` (512-d) and `embed-large-v2` (1536-d) in the same workload and then attempts to batch results into a single index flush.

Arjun: Two problems that explain tail spikes and errors:
1) max_batch_size was set high (128) for that workspace, so some requests wait to fill and also cause larger kernel invocations that increase p99 when there is variability in sequence length.
2) dynamic routing allowed cross-model packing; when the model chooser fell back to a different variant under capacity pressure, customer saw mixed dims.

Maya: Customer asked for immediate mitigation steps they can apply client-side while we fix server policy.

Arjun: Suggested quick mitigations:
- Pin `model` parameter to the specific model (`embed-small-v1`) in all requests. Do not rely on auto model routing.
- Set client `max_batch_size` to 32 or lower.
- Set client `batch_timeout_ms` to 20 (or lower for low-latency SLOs).
- Stop mixing model ids in a single batch; enforce per-model batch queues.

Elena: Sent these steps to the customer, they applied pinning and lowered batch size. Reported p99 dropped from ~1.2s to ~140ms within 10 minutes and dimension errors disappeared. :tada:

Arjun: Longer term fixes we should track in eng-ml:
- Reject coalescing across incompatible model output dims in the batching layer (explicit compatibility check)
- Add a runtime config `enforce_model_homogeneity` per-tenant default true
- Auto-adjust `max_batch_size` by observed sequence-length distribution; prefer smaller batches for skewed workloads
- Improve observability: surface per-model embedding_dim in console and expose a per-route metric for `mixed_model_coalesces`

Nate: Quick change I pushed to a feature-flagged branch: `batcher: check_output_dim_compatibility=true`. Rolling to staging. CI-Bot: deploy logs

CI-Bot: deployment redwood/batcher v2026.03.15-ff: SUCCESS to staging

Arjun: Next steps for support:
- Keep customer on pinned model until flag is stable
- Roll the compatibility check to prod behind a safe rollout (canary on 5% orgs)
- Add an incident doc template for embedding-dimension mismatches (repro steps, mitigation)

Maya: Customer is happy for now. I'll keep the ticket open and watch for regressions. Closing loop: thank you everyone. :heart:
